paragraphs: People who rely on turn-by-turn navigation apps often report that they cannot find their way around cities they have lived in for years. This is sometimes taken as evidence that the apps have eroded their sense of direction. A more modest interpretation is available. When a device issues instructions, the traveler need only obey them, and nothing requires the traveler to notice landmarks or to form a mental map of the route; the knowledge that unaided navigation would have produced never gets built. In that case the apps would not have damaged an existing ability so much as prevented one from developing. The two accounts predict different things: only the first implies that people who once navigated well will do worse after adopting the apps.
